what_this_measures: Precision and recall of orchestrator/grounding.py's check_grounding() on a hand-labelled adversarial set. Positive class = a number that is fabricated and should be flagged. Fully offline and deterministic — no LLM involved in either the checker or this score.

per_case.why: A wholly grounded report. Any flag here is a false positive.
The documented tolerance rule: a report may round a source value to its own precision. +0.26 against 0.2622 must pass.
The commonest fabrication shape: a plausible but invented metric.
The real fabrication caught in Phase 3: correct-in-the-world classification bands recited from training data and cited to a document that does not contain them.
Materially different at the report's own precision. A checker that let this through would be useless — this is the hard case.
A fabricated '4-month horizon' must not be accepted merely because '4' appears inside the source value 0.0438. This is why the checker enforces number boundaries rather than substring matching.

The Phase-3.1 bug's signature: a non-text metadata block stringified into the report body. The checker's behaviour was correct — those digits are genuinely unverifiable — so every one of them is a true positive.
A count inflated from 7 to 17 — grounded-looking, materially wrong.
The sourced coefficient reported exactly as the table holds it.

The Phase-4 failure mode: asked about crop impact, a model supplies a confident percentage from general agronomic knowledge. KNOWN FALSE NEGATIVE — see PERCENT_FRACTION_DEFECT below. Kept in the set as a failing case rather than removed or worked around.
Scaling a single anchor point into a per-degree rate — forbidden by the yield table's own caveat, and it produces a number that exists in no source.
Years, horizon labels and index names carry no measured claim and must never be flagged — false positives here would make the checker's output unreadable.
A source fraction 0.0766 reported as 7.66% is the same quantity.
